_bridge_mode_docs._what: Controls which 32-bit processes the bridge engages with.
_bridge_mode_docs.whitelist: Bridge ONLY the processes listed under 'targets'. Default mode. Precise control.
_bridge_mode_docs.blacklist: Bridge ALL 32-bit processes on the system EXCEPT those listed under 'blacklist'. Use this to extend every 32-bit application at once.
_bridge_mode_docs._et_derivation: whitelist D = explicit inclusion set. blacklist D = all 32-bit minus exclusion set. Both describe the same P from opposite D-directions. ET Identification Principle: the same P (all 32-bit processes) with complementary D-sets.

_blacklist_comment: List exe names (case-insensitive) that should NOT be bridged.
Recommended entries: critical system processes that must not be modified.
This list is entirely under your control — no entries are hardcoded.
Example: your antivirus, anti-cheat engines, or trusted 32-bit system tools.

ipc._comment: IPC tuning — derived from ET: buffer = hd×S = 4096×12 = 49152; queue = S² = 144

logging._comment: Logging configuration. Log is always written to disk (immediate flush). Survives crashes.
_crash_coverage: faulthandler          — C-level crashes, segfaults, stack overflow, SIGABRT
atexit                — final flush + error registry summary on any exit
Windows SEH filter    — DLL-level crashes from injected code
_path_resolution: file = null or absent  → log placed in same directory as ET32_Bridge.exe (default)
file = 'et32_bridge.log' → relative → resolved from exe directory
dir  = 'C:\\Logs'           → log placed in this directory as et32_bridge.log

_targets_comment: Used when bridge.mode = 'whitelist'. Listed processes are bridged. Others are ignored.

targets._comment: Example: 32-bit game needing >4GB VRAM and large file maps
Example: legacy 32-bit CAD tool needing extended memory
